transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

Based on the symptoms you described, here is the diagnosis and solution:

### Diagnosis: Error Code Er03
On AEG (and many other European brands like Electrolux/Hotpoint) induction hobs, Er03 typically indicates a "System Overheat" or "Internal Temperature Too High" fault.

The fact that your pasta boiled over just before the error occurred is the likely cause. Here’s why:
1.  Liquid Spillage: Boiling-over liquid can seep into the control panel vents or internal components of the hob.
2.  Short Circuit/Interference: The conductive liquid (especially if it contains salt from pasta water) may have caused a temporary short circuit in the sensors or control board.
3.  Overheating Trigger: Some models interpret unusual sensor readings or moisture ingress as an overheating condition and shut down to protect the electronics, displaying Er03.

---

### Immediate Steps to Fix It

#### ✅ Step 1: Power Down Completely
• Turn off the hob using its power button (if it still responds).
• Switch off the circuit breaker/fuse for the kitchen or specifically for the hob at your main electrical panel.
  (This is crucial because induction hobs draw significant power, and a simple "off" may not fully reset the internal capacitor-based memory.)

#### ✅ Step 2: Clean Thoroughly
• Once powered down, carefully wipe away all spilled pasta water from the surface, control panel, and around the edges of the hob.
• Use a dry microfiber cloth to ensure no moisture remains in the seams or vents.
• If you suspect liquid got inside, leave it open/accessible for air circulation if possible (do not use heat guns or hairdryers on high heat).

#### ✅ Step 3: Wait for Cool-Down & Reset
• Leave the hob powered off for at least 15–30 minutes. This allows:
• Any residual moisture to evaporate.
• Internal components to cool down completely.
• The control board to fully reset.

#### ✅ Step 4: Restore Power & Test
• Turn the circuit breaker back on.
• Turn on the hob normally.
• Try using one burner at a low power setting with a suitable pan (not empty).
• If it works without error, you’re good to go.

---

### ⚠️ If Er03 Returns Immediately
If the error comes back right after restoring power:
1. Moisture Intrusion: Liquid likely penetrated deeper into the electronics. You may need to leave it powered off for several hours (or even overnight) to dry out completely.
2. Component Damage: If drying doesn’t help, the spill may have caused a permanent short in the control board or temperature sensor. In this case:
• Contact AEG Support or a qualified appliance technician.
• Do not attempt to open the hob yourself unless you are certified, as induction hobs contain high-voltage capacitors that can retain charge even when unplugged.

---

### 🔮 Prevention Tips for Future Use
• Avoid overfilling pots beyond 2/3 capacity.
• Use a larger pot or lower heat setting when boiling starchy foods (like pasta) to prevent rapid foaming.
• Wipe up spills immediately after cooling down to prevent residue buildup.

Let me know if the error persists after this reset!
Ok, I wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes. It works again now, all four zones fine. A wooden spoon was resting on the edge of the controls too, I moved it. Is that all it was?

It is highly likely that both factors contributed to the issue, though the boiling-over liquid was probably the primary trigger. Here’s why:

### 1. The Boiling-Over Liquid (Primary Cause)
Induction hobs are sensitive to moisture on or near their control surfaces. When pasta water (which contains starch and salt) boiled over, it likely seeped into the seams around the touch controls. This can cause two problems:
• Short Circuit: Saltwater is conductive. If it bridged contacts in the control panel, it could send false signals or trigger a safety shutdown.
• Sensor Interference: The moisture may have temporarily confused the temperature or proximity sensors, causing the hob to think there was an internal overheating fault (Er03).

### 2. The Wooden Spoon (Secondary/Contributing Factor)
Wood is not conductive like metal, so it wouldn’t cause a short circuit. However:
• Heat Insulation: If the spoon was resting on or near the control panel while the hob was running, it could have trapped heat against the plastic surface. Induction hobs monitor their own internal temperature; if external objects block ventilation or add insulation, the system might misinterpret this as an overheating condition.
• Physical Pressure: If the spoon pressed down on the touch controls, it could have inadvertently activated a function (like locking the panel) while the hob was already in a sensitive state due to the spillage.

### Why It Worked After Resetting
When you switched off the power at the wall for 5 minutes:
• Any residual moisture from the spill had time to evaporate or dry out slightly.
• The control board fully reset, clearing the temporary fault memory.
• The heat trapped by the spoon dissipated once the hob was powered down.

### Recommendations to Prevent Recurrence
1. Keep Controls Clear: Always ensure no utensils (wooden spoons, spatulas, etc.) are resting on or near the control panel while the hob is in use. This prevents accidental activation and heat buildup.
2. Clean Spills Immediately: Wipe up any boiling-over liquids as soon as they happen to prevent seepage into the controls. Use a dry cloth after wiping with a damp one to ensure no moisture remains.
3. Monitor for Recurrence: If Er03 happens again without any spills or objects on the controls, it could indicate an internal sensor issue or failing component, and you may need professional service.

For now, since all four zones are working fine after the reset, you’re likely good to go! Just be mindful of keeping the control area clear and dry.
